summary: @onereach/si-root preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes obfuscated payload
details: The package's preinstall hook runs `node setup.mjs`, which downloads the Bun runtime (v1.3.13) from oven-sh/bun GitHub releases into a temp directory, marks it executable, and uses it to execute `math_init.js`, a 727KB heavily-obfuscated JavaScript blob shipped in the tarball. This runs automatically on `npm install`. Both setup.mjs and math_init.js use obfuscator.io-style identifier mangling and rotated string-array decoders (`_0x488df8` identifiers, split-string property lookups, `WV8StW` shift routine, large hex-literal arrays) that hide the payload's behavior from Node-based static inspection. The package presents itself as a Vue 'step-inputs' UI component library, a purpose that has no need for a second language runtime or an opaque math-named executable at install time. Using a freshly-fetched alternate runtime to execute an obfuscated bundled payload at preinstall is the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern: the Bun invocation bypasses Node instrumentation and delivers unreviewable code onto the installer's machine during a normal `npm install`.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
